Hello! My name is KG and I am a recent PhD graduate from the University of Virginia under Ken Ono. Mathematically, I'm interested in combinatorics and number theory; technically, I've been hobby programming for about fifteen years now, and have been using (read: trying to get familiar with the depth and idiosyncrasy of) Lean for the last six months. (website and GitHub)

I'm eager to try to expand Mathlib's infrastructure for integer partitions, and I hope to draft some PRs soon concerning the introductory elements of Andrews' Theory of Partitions, especially with the recent attention being given to the q-series side. Modular forms are also on my radar, though I think the implementation and API details there require much more care (which I hope I can foster in due time).
Welcome! Mathlib already has some API for docs#ModularForm. If you are interested on expanding it, it would be a good idea to discuss with @Chris Birkbeck first.
Yes welcome! We do have quite a bit on modular forms now, both in mathlib and in external repos. What things about modular forms are you interested in?

@Chris Birkbeck I've been trying to keep an eye on the state of foundational elements like the valence formula (which you seem to have recently managed to skirt around complex integration to obtain?) and the eta function (and other infrastructure used/developed by the sphere packing project), the latter as means of entry to partition theoretic results like Rademacher's theorem. I'd also like to see a Poincare series API developed, and as a distant goal my interests lie in harmonic Maass forms.

So I do now have a proof of the valence formula done by Claude, but it still far from being ready for mathlib, but yes we managed to avoid it and prove the dimension formula via another route. You can have a look at my repo here and the branches to see where I'm at with this and other modular form stuff (like Hecke operatiors, strong multiplicity one, etc). But partition results would be great as would more Poincare series API (we have Theta series already and some API here). Nothing about Maass forms.
Thanks, I'll take a look at your repo.

I've opened my first PR linking partitions and Young diagrams: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/39722. Comments on the API or how I've made all the wrong implementation decisions would be greatly appreciated.
